about: Cross-language conformance vectors. Every binding builds these inputs, runs them through the C ABI, and must reproduce each sha256 exactly. The Zig suite (tests/golden.zig) checks them against the library itself. Inputs are integers over a power of two, so every language constructs bit-identical floats. Seeds are hex strings because some exceed 2^53, which a JSON number cannot carry exactly.
input: x[r][j] = ((r*7919 + j*104729 + salt) mod 2001 - 1000) / 1024, as float32, row-major, 0 <= r < rows, 0 <= j < dim
index_hash: sha256 of zq_index_serialize output after zq_index_create(config), zq_index_calibrate(all rows) if calibrate, and zq_index_add(all rows)
codec_hash: sha256 of the zq_codec_encode codes for all rows, followed by the norms as little-endian float32
